title: Urbanisation and Urban Challenges
summary: Why people move to cities (push and pull factors), urban land-use zones, informal settlements, and the problems and solutions of fast-growing cities in South Africa.

notes.text: The increase in the percentage of a country's population living in towns and cities.

More than half of the world's people now live in urban areas. In South Africa about **two-thirds** of people live in towns and cities. Gauteng, the smallest province by area, has the largest population.

notes.title: Calculating the level of urbanisation
notes.problem: A country has 60 million people, 40 million of whom live in cities. What percentage is urbanised?

notes.text: The movement of people from the countryside to towns and cities. It is the main cause of urbanisation, together with natural increase (more births than deaths) in cities.

notes.title: Sorting push and pull
notes.problem: Classify: drought on the farm, jobs in town, few schools in the village, better hospitals in town.
steps: Push factors drive people away from rural areas: drought and few schools.
Pull factors attract people to cities: jobs and better hospitals.
notes.answer: Push: drought, few schools. Pull: jobs, better hospitals.

rows: The centre: offices, banks, shops, government buildings; tall buildings; very high land values; busy traffic
Factories and warehouses, usually near railways, highways or harbours
Large houses with gardens on the outskirts, often in pleasant areas
Shacks built by people without formal housing, often on the edges of the city
Where the city meets the countryside: smallholdings, new suburbs, shopping malls

notes.label: Apartheid legacy
notes.text: Under the **Group Areas Act**, black South Africans were forced to live in townships far from city centres and jobs. Many people still travel long distances and spend a large part of their income on transport.

items: **Housing shortages** and the growth of **informal settlements** with poor services.
**Unemployment**: there are not enough jobs for everyone, so many work in the **informal sector** (street vendors, spaza shops).
**Pressure on services**: water, sanitation, electricity, schools and clinics.
**Crime** and health problems such as the spread of disease in overcrowded areas.
**Urban sprawl**: cities spread outwards over farmland and natural areas.
Government housing programmes (RDP houses) and **upgrading** informal settlements with water, toilets and electricity.
Improved **public transport**, such as bus rapid transit (Rea Vaya in Johannesburg, MyCiTi in Cape Town) and the Gautrain.
**Rural development**: creating jobs and services in rural areas so fewer people need to move.
Supporting small businesses and the informal sector.
Building denser housing closer to jobs, and protecting green spaces.
